name: Cho Oyu Expedition
sub_region: Solukhumbu District, Koshi Province (Khumbu Himal, NW of Everest) and Tingri County, Tibet Autonomous Region, China

difficulty.technical_grade: Tibet NW Ridge: PD (operator assessments). Nepal SW Face: AD/D (operator assessments); not a standard commercial line
difficulty.notes: Sixth-highest mountain. Almost all commercial ascents have used the Northwest Ridge from Tibet (moderate snow, a short Yellow Band rock step, fixed ropes). The Nepal (south/southwest) side is steeper, with ice cliffs and limited infrastructure; ExplorersWeb (Aug 2026) states it is not suitable for commercial expeditions despite Nepali operators trying to open it. First ascent (19 Oct 1954) was the Tichy route, West Ridge/West Face approached from the south via Nangpa La.

duration_days.basis: Historically full trip Kathmandu-Kathmandu on the Tibet NW Ridge when CTMA permits foreigners
duration_days.notes: Tibet programmes are commonly 40-45 days (drive Kerung/Kyirong-Tingri-Chinese BC-ABC, then rotations). Nepal-side operator listings of about 50 days exist; a reconstructed commercial SW-Face itinerary was not found. Tibet-side Cho Oyu was closed to foreign expeditions for 2026 (CTMA; reports cover autumn 2026 and, in Tourism Times, all of 2026). Confirm CTMA status before any departure.

max_altitude_point: Cho Oyu summit (Himalayan Database 8,188 m; some operators still print 8,201 m)
start_point: Kathmandu (Tibet: overland via Timure/Kerung-Kyirong when the border and CTMA are open; Nepal-side: Lukla)

itinerary.route: Arrive Kathmandu; Tibet visa / CTMA paperwork (when the route is open) or Nepal DoT briefing for a Nepal-side attempt
itinerary.notes: Tibet itinerary below is the historical commercial programme. It was not available to foreigners in 2026.

itinerary.route: Drive Kathmandu - Timure - Kerung/Kyirong (about 2,700 m) - Tingri (about 4,300 m); rest/acclimatise at Tingri
itinerary.notes: Alternative when allowed: Kathmandu-Lhasa flight then drive west. Rasuwagadhi-Kerung road was reported shut after flooding in late August 2026.

itinerary.route: Drive Tingri - Chinese Base Camp (about 5,100-5,200 m); rest; move via Middle Camp (about 5,300-5,400 m) to Advance Base Camp (about 5,700 m) on the Gyabrag Glacier
itinerary.notes: ABC is the working camp for the NW Ridge.

itinerary.route: Rotations: ABC - Camp 1 (about 6,400 m, foot of the NW ridge) - Camp 2 (about 7,100-7,200 m) - optional Camp 3 / high camp below the Yellow Band (about 7,450-7,500 m) - rest at ABC
itinerary.notes: Ice-cliff step between C1 and C2; Yellow Band rock on the upper mountain; summit plateau to the true summit.

itinerary.route: Summit window: high camp - summit 8,188 m - ABC; pack; drive Tingri - Kerung - Kathmandu
itinerary.walking_hours: Summit day from C2 or C3

itinerary.route: Lukla - Namche - Gokyo or Thame valley toward Nangpa La (about 5,700-5,806 m) / south base camp area (operator figures 5,300-5,419 m) - SW Face camps
itinerary.notes: Nangpa La / Thame side enters Khumbu Pasang Lhamu ward 5 (restricted-area permit). Crossing into Tibet without CTMA papers is illegal. No reliable commercial camp sequence for the SW Face was found in this research.

best_seasons.notes: Cho Oyu was historically an autumn first-8,000 m peak on the Tibet side. Spring 2026 and autumn 2026 Tibet access for foreigners did not open. Nepal-side weather windows follow the usual Khumbu spring/autumn pattern if a private team is fielded.

permits.name: Nepal Department of Tourism climbing royalty - other mountains above 8,000 m (Nepal-side Cho Oyu)
permits.fee: USD 3,000 per person spring; USD 1,500 autumn; USD 750 winter/summer
permits.applies_to: foreign climbers on a Nepal expedition permit

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per team) - other 8,000 m in Khumbu, Nepal-side
Sagarmatha National Park entry (Nepal approach)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person per entry (SAARC NPR 1,500)
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals on a Nepal-side approach

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Trek-Card (Nepal approach)
permits.fee: NPR 3,000 per person (SAARC and Chinese nationals NPR 2,000)

permits.name: Restricted area permit - Solukhumbu, Khumbu Pasang Lhamu ward 5 (Nangpa La / Thame valley)
permits.fee: USD 20 per person per week for the first 4 weeks; USD 25 per week beyond. Immigration has stated expedition-permit holders must still obtain the RAP but do not pay its fee (same wording used for other restricted areas).
permits.applies_to: foreign nationals on a Nepal-side Nangpa/Thame approach
permits.status: VERIFIED (fee table); fee-waiver for climbers UNVERIFIED in 2026 on a live Immigration page

permits.name: China-Tibet Mountaineering Association (CTMA) Cho Oyu permit and Tibet visa (Tibet NW Ridge)
permits.fee: Not a Nepal DoT fee. Operator/trade reports have cited about USD 9,300 per foreign climber plus staff charges; no official CTMA tariff was opened in this research.
permits.applies_to: foreign climbers on the Tibet side
permits.status: UNVERIFIED (amount); VERIFIED that foreigners were barred in 2026

guide_requirements: Nepal-side 8,000 m: Sixth Amendment solo ban; at least one mountain guide or high-altitude worker per two members; liaison officer; staff insurance minimums. Tibet-side: CTMA rules and a Chinese liaison officer when the peak is open; Nepali agencies cannot substitute a Nepal permit for a Tibet climb. Nangpa La approaches also fall under Nepal restricted-area guide rules.

flights: Optional Kathmandu-Lhasa when Tibet is open
drives: Kathmandu - Timure - Kerung/Kyirong - Tingri - Chinese Base Camp (Tibet programme)
logistics.notes: Tibet: hotels to Tingri, tents at Chinese BC and ABC. Nepal-side: teahouses to Gokyo/Thame, then camping. Icefall Doctors' fee does not apply (no Khumbu Icefall on either normal Cho Oyu line).

highlights: Sixth-highest mountain, 8,188 m, on the Nepal-Tibet border
Historically the most accessible commercial 8,000 m peak (Tibet NW Ridge) when China issues permits
First ascent 19 October 1954: Herbert Tichy, Sepp (Josef) Jöchler and Pasang Dawa Lama, W Ridge/W Face from the south via Nangpa La
Gokyo lakes / Nangpa La trade route on Nepal approaches
risks: Political/permit closure of the Tibet route (in force for foreigners in 2026)
Altitude jump on the Tibet road approach (Tingri to 5,700 m ABC)
Yellow Band and summit-plateau navigation; false summit before the true high point
Nepal SW Face: ice cliffs, crevasses, limited rescue and no established commercial fixed-rope operation

acclimatization.notes: Tibet programmes rely on staged driving then ABC rotations. A Nepal-side team would acclimatise on the Gokyo/Thame walk-in plus mountain rotations; no standard rotation count was found.

unverified: CTMA permit tariff (USD 9,300 figure is trade/operator reporting only).
Whether the Tibet ban is autumn-2026-only or all of 2026 (Tourism Times vs ExplorersWeb wording differs; both agree autumn 2026 is closed).
Spring 2027 CTMA reopening — not announced as of this research.
Height 8,188 m vs 8,201 m (Kielkowski / some operators).
Tibet camp altitudes vary (Chinese BC 4,950-5,200 m; ABC 5,650-5,800 m; C1 6,400 m; C2 7,100-7,200 m; C3 7,450-7,500 m).
Any currently operating Nepal-side commercial SW Face programme (none confirmed; ExplorersWeb says not commercially suitable).
RAP fee waiver for expedition-permit holders: stated on Immigration pages used in 2026-10-20 regulations research; the live Immigration trekking-permit URL returned 404 on 2026-10-22.
